nodes.description: Migraine aura is driven by cortical spreading depolarization, a propagating wave of neuronal and glial depolarization that generates transient focal neurological symptoms and provides the major mechanistic substrate for aura.

evidence.snippet: The pivotal role of cortical spreading depression (CSD) as a mechanism underlying aura has been widely supported by a large body of studies.

evidence.reference_title: The mysterious link between migraine aura and migraine headache.
evidence.snippet: Cortical spreading depolarization (SD), recognized as the mechanism underlying aura symptoms, has been shown to trigger head pain through activation of trigeminal nociceptors in animal models.

nodes.description: Hyperhomocysteinemia injures the vascular endothelium; the resulting endothelial dysfunction provides the route that can activate the trigeminovascular system and underlies the microvascular and ischemic susceptibility of migraine with aura.

evidence.snippet: Hyperhomocysteinemia produce endothelial cell injury, which may activate trigeminovascular system (TVS), resulting in an inflammatory action in the meninges and dilation of the large cerebral vessels.

nodes.description: The MTHFR C677T (677T) allele lowers enzyme activity and mildly raises plasma total homocysteine, producing the mild hyperhomocysteinemia that provides a vascular route to migraine-with-aura susceptibility.

nodes.description: Reduced two-pore-domain (K2P) potassium channel activity links the KCNK18 (TRESK) migraine-with-aura mutation to sensory-neuron hyperexcitability. The disease-relevant effect of the F139WfsX24 frameshift is downregulation of the related TREK1/TREK2 channels, increasing the excitability of trigeminal and dorsal root ganglion sensory neurons rather than acting on cortex directly.
